entries.topic: The 2013 interim deal, the JCPOA, Resolution 2231, Netanyahu's opposition, AIPAC's campaign, IAEA verification 2016-2019

claims.text: Joint Plan of Action dated 24 November 2013; from 20 January 2014 IAEA confirmed Iran halted 20% enrichment; Iran capped enrichment at 5%, froze centrifuge numbers, diluted or converted its 20% stockpile, froze Arak work; US/EU suspended some sanctions; IAEA monthly reports noted implementation; Kerry said at the November 2014 extension Iran had complied

JCPOA limits: enrichment to 3.67% for 15 years; enriched stockpile 300 kg for 15 years; 5,060 IR-1 centrifuges enriching only at Natanz for 10 years (pre-deal >19,000 installed, ~10,200 enriching); no enrichment at Fordow for 15 years; Arak redesigned to 20 MWt, core made inoperable, plutonium output from >7 kg/yr to ~1 kg/yr; Additional Protocol; 24-day procedure for contested access (14+7+3); breakout from 2-3 months to >12 months; sunsets at years 5, 8, 10, 15, 20, 25
UNSC Resolution 2231 adopted unanimously 20 July 2015; endorses JCPOA, ten-year duration, snapback process for UN sanctions; Iran said it would cease performing commitments if sanctions restored
Netanyahu, 14 July 2015: 'this agreement is an historic mistake for the world'; 'Far-reaching concessions have been made'

Speaker Boehner invited Netanyahu to address Congress without consulting the White House (January 2015); WH press secretary Earnest called it a 'departure from protocol'; Obama would not meet him, citing the Israeli election

Netanyahu, Congress, 3 March 2015: 'this is a bad deal'; 'It doesn't block Iran's path to the bomb; it paves Iran's path to the bomb'; 'It would be a farewell to arms control'; restrictions should stay 'until Iran's aggression ends'
WSJ reported (March 2015) Israel spied on the talks and briefed lawmakers; Israeli officials denied spying, saying details came from French officials
AIPAC backed Citizens for a Nuclear Free Iran (launched July 2015) running a multimillion-dollar national TV/digital campaign; advisory board Bayh, Begich, Landrieu, Lieberman, Berkley
Politico reported a planned $20 million ad buy in 30-40 states
LobeLog/Clifton: AIPAC committed $20-40m; at least $14.5m in TV ads per FCC filings to end Sept 2015; CNFI raised nearly $30m per JTA's Kampeas; AIEF raised >$80m in 2015
Senate vote 10 September 2015 58-42 on disapproval resolution; 60 needed; Democrats filibustered; measure failed
Iran shipped ~25,000 lb of low-enriched material to Russia, late December 2015; Kerry: 'one of the most significant steps'; breakout said moved from 2-3 months to 6-9 months at that stage
IAEA Implementation Day statement 16 January 2016: inspectors 'verified that Iran has carried out all measures required under the JCPOA'
Amano 9 May 2018: 'the IAEA can confirm that the nuclear-related commitments are being implemented by Iran'; 'the world's most robust nuclear verification regime'
AP 31 May 2019: IAEA quarterly report said Iran 'continues to stay within the limitations'; inspectors had access to all sites needed
J Street ran a full-page NYT ad (23 July 2015) urging Congress not to 'sabotage' the deal, part of what it called a 'multimillion dollar campaign' with TV ads and a website

entries.topic: The 2018 archive presentation, US withdrawal and maximum pressure, Iran's breaches from 2019, later assessments of the withdrawal, 2025 status

claims.text: Netanyahu, Defense Ministry, Tel Aviv, 30 April 2018: 'Iran lied. Big time.'; 'Fifty-five thousand pages. Another 55,000 files on 183 CDs'; Israel obtained 'half a ton' of material 'a few weeks ago'; 'Project Amad'; 'five Hiroshima bombs'; 'the Iran deal ... is based on lies'; Trump to decide 'in a few days'

Pompeo, 30 April 2018: 'The documents show that Iran had a secret nuclear-weapons program for years'; UK: 'We have never been naive'; Germany: 'It was for this reason the nuclear accord was signed'; IAEA 1 May 2018 recalled its 2015 finding of 'no credible indications of activities in Iran relevant to the development of a nuclear explosive device after 2009'; Zarif: 'How convenient', 'a rehash of old allegations'

Trump, 8 May 2018: 'the United States will withdraw from the Iran nuclear deal'; 'decaying and rotten structure'; 'highest level of economic sanction'; 'At the heart of the Iran deal was a giant fiction'; cited Israel's published documents; called sunsets 'totally unacceptable'; deal 'fails to address' ballistic missiles
Netanyahu, 8 May 2018, called Trump's decision 'correct, wise and courageous'

Pompeo, Heritage Foundation, May 2018: 12 demands incl. stop enrichment, 'unqualified access to all sites', end support for Hezbollah, Hamas, Houthis; 'These will be the strongest sanctions in history'; Rouhani: 'Who are you to decide for Iran and the world?'
US sanctions reimposed in two waves: August 2018 (dollar purchases, gold, metals, autos) and 5 November 2018 (oil, NIOC, shipping, central bank transactions, insurance)
22 April 2019 Pompeo said oil waivers (eight granted after reimposition) would not be renewed after 2 May; 'Our goal has been to get countries to cease importing Iranian oil entirely'

Iran SNSC 8 May 2019: citing JCPOA paragraphs 26 and 36, Iran stopped observing limits on enriched uranium and heavy water stocks; gave remaining parties 60 days 'to fulfil their obligations, especially in banking and oil'; threatened further steps

1 July 2019: Zarif said Iran 'crossed the 300-kilogramme limit'; IAEA confirmed; Zarif cited paragraph 36 and said steps reversible; White House: restore 'no enrichment' standard, maximum pressure maintained; Netanyahu called it 'significant step toward making a nuclear weapon'

Iran enriched to 4.5% from July 2019; resumed enrichment at Fordow November 2019; 5 January 2020 said no limits on centrifuge numbers; Zarif: steps 'reversible upon effective implementation of reciprocal obligations'; demanded banking and oil sales; EU's Borrell regretted
16 April 2021 Iran began 60% enrichment at Natanz after sabotage Tehran blamed on Israel (Israel did not claim it); Iran said medical purposes
Vienna talks to revive the JCPOA began April 2021; EU submitted 'final' text 8 August 2022; Iran demanded assurances on sanctions and safeguards; US said it was up to Iran

IAEA May 2025 report (as of 17 May 2025): 408.6 kg uranium enriched to 60%; total enriched stock 9,247.6 kg; ~21,900 centrifuges installed incl. ~14,689 advanced; Fordow producing 60% since Nov 2022; no Additional Protocol since 23 Feb 2021; continuity of knowledge lost

CRS: IAEA verified Iran exceeding JCPOA limits from July 2019; Iran stopped JCPOA verification and Additional Protocol Feb 2021; E3 triggered snapback 28 Aug 2025; UN sanctions reimposed 27 Sept 2025; Iran, Russia, China letter 18 Oct 2025 argued snapback invalid and 2231 terminated; inspectors withdrawn after June 2025 strikes

Eisenkot (IDF chief 2015-19), Maariv interview reported 28 January 2022: withdrawal 'a strategic mistake'; 'No one spoke with the security establishment'; only Netanyahu, Cohen, Dermer handled it; Mossad pushed for withdrawal; Iran did not resume enrichment beyond limits until 2019
Ya'alon (Haaretz, Nov 2021): 'the main mistake was the withdrawal from the agreement'; Cintrinowicz: 'Everything started going haywire when Trump left the agreement'

New Lines: Ya'alon late Nov 2021 'a historic mistake'; Pardo late Nov 2021 'disaster'; Yadlin Aug 2021 Channel 12 'The path that Netanyahu led got Iran extremely close to a bomb'; Bennett thanked Trump for withdrawal; Netanyahu in May 2018 hailed it as 'historic move'
Biden CNN op-ed 13 Sept 2020 called Trump's policy 'a dangerous failure', pledged to rejoin if Iran returned to compliance

entries.topic: Audit re-verification of JCPOA terms, vote, lobbying and snapback

claims.text: Clifton: AIPAC 'committed to spending $20-40 million in television commercials' (figure linked to Vox, 4 Sept 2015, not to filings); at least $14.5m in TV ads per a LobeLog review of FCC filings at the end of September 2015; AIPAC did not respond to a request for comment

JPOA sanctions relief: US and EU suspended sanctions on petrochemicals and gold/precious metals; the US alone on autos; US allowed spare parts and repair services for civilian aircraft; Kerry at the 24 Nov 2014 extension said Iran had 'complied with all of its obligations' (ACA paraphrase)

CRS: E3 invoked snapback in an 28 August 2025 letter; UN sanctions reimposed 27 September 2025; Russia-China resolution of 26 September 2025 not adopted; China, Iran, Russia letter of 18 October 2025 called the step invalid
